info.name: ENVISION MCP OAuth
info.description: OAuth 2.0 endpoints for the ENVISION MCP server (Controllers/McpOAuthController.cs). These are inert unless the EnableMcpOAuth parameter is True; while off they return 404 and the MCP endpoint keeps its HTTP Basic + session-cookie behaviour. The discovery, authorize, token and register endpoints are intentionally not behind the /mcp bearer guard so a client can obtain a token. ENVISION is both the authorization server and the resource server, so no external identity provider is required. Set collection variables base_url, username and password before use; use http://127.0.0.1 for base_url. The password grant is for machine-to-machine callers and maps directly onto ENVISION credentials via LoginHelper. Interactive clients use the authorization-code + PKCE flow via /mcp/oauth/authorize, which is a browser sign-in page and is not scripted here.

request.description: RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata: issuer, authorize/token/registration endpoints, supported grant types and PKCE methods. Returns 404 when EnableMcpOAuth is False.
RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata: points the client at the authorization server. Returns 404 when EnableMcpOAuth is False.
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration. Returns a generated client_id for a public (PKCE) client.
Resource-owner password grant for machine-to-machine callers. On success the test script stores access_token in the mcp_access_token collection variable.
Calls the MCP endpoint with the bearer token obtained above, proving OAuth authentication works end to end.
